questions.answer: Not particularly well. I'll join in at weddings and celebrations, which is impossible to avoid here, but I'd never call myself a dancer. I do it purely for the fun of the moment rather than any real [[flair]].

questions.q: Is dancing popular in your country?
questions.answer: Very much so, especially at weddings and cultural festivals. Classical and folk dance are also taught formally, and during Pohela Boishakh you often see groups performing in [[vibrant]] traditional costumes.

questions.q: Did you learn to dance when you were a child?
questions.answer: No, dance lessons were more common for girls where I grew up. My younger sister took classical dance classes for a few years, though, and she was genuinely [[graceful]], unlike her brother.

questions.q: Do you enjoy watching other people dance?
questions.answer: Definitely, especially skilled performers. I once watched a Manipuri dance performance at a cultural event, and the control and precision were [[mesmerising]]. It's a completely different experience from watching relatives dance at a wedding.

questions.q: Do you think dancing is a good way to keep fit?
questions.answer: I'd say it's one of the best, because people forget they're exercising. It works the whole body and lifts your mood at the same time, so it's far easier to [[stick with]] than a dull gym routine.
